question: What does the World Bank's 2026 poverty report actually show about India, and why do economists still disagree?

theme.label: Economy and public money
readerQuestions: What is the headline economic number?
Is this a total number or a per-person number?
How much of the story is prices, exchange rates, or GDP share?
What does this explain about household life?

plannedCharts.title: India largely cleared the $3/day floor by 2024, yet 78.8% of the population still lives below the $8.30/day threshold

series.label: Societal poverty rate ($3.00 to $4.27/day dynamic line)

plannedCharts.subtitle: World Bank 2026 Poverty, Prosperity, and Planet Report lined-up headcount rates (1990-2030) and PIP Societal Poverty Rate (1993-2023) · 2021 PPP
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: Shows all four World Bank poverty benchmarks together from 1990 to 2030 so readers see why celebrating the end of $3/day poverty misses four-fifths of the population.

plannedCharts.title: A hypothetical 10% real consumption loss lifts the $4.20 poverty share from 14.9% to 23.2%
plannedCharts.subtitle: Same 2024 population bins, before and after a hypothetical uniform consumption loss · 2021 PPP · approximately 0.1 percentage-point resolution
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: Tests how much consumption security sits just above each poverty line.

plannedCharts.title: Among Indians below $8.30, consumption averages 34.1% short of the line
plannedCharts.unit: % of poverty line, among those below it
plannedCharts.subtitle: Average consumption shortfall among people below each line · HCES 2023-24 · 2021 PPP · PIP September 2026
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: Headcounts count people below the line; this measures how far below it those people live.

plannedCharts.title: The Prosperity Gap is 6.72 in Jharkhand and 3.16 in Goa
plannedCharts.subtitle: World Bank Global Subnational Atlas of Poverty (GSAP) Fall 2026 · average shortfall factor from the $28/day prosperity standard across all 36 states and UTs · HCES 2023-24
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: Maps the World Bank's new flagship Prosperity Gap indicator across all 36 Indian states and union territories for the first time.

plannedCharts.title: Young children are more likely to live below $8.30 a day in every state and union territory
plannedCharts.subtitle: Ages 0-5 versus all ages, 14 selected states · SPID direct HCES 2023-24 estimates · source reference year 2023.58
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: Adds a demographic comparison within each state rather than another map of average poverty.

plannedCharts.title: The 2021 PPP revision paradox: Updating global prices raised India's 2023 extreme poverty rate to 2.57% while cutting $4.20 poverty to 16.12%
plannedCharts.subtitle: Indian survey-year poverty headcount rates in the September 2026 PIP release under the 2017 PPP lines ($2.15, $3.65, $6.85) vs 2021 PPP lines ($3.00, $4.20, $8.30)
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: Explains the counter-intuitive arithmetic of the World Bank's switch from 2017 ICP PPP to 2021 ICP PPP: extreme poverty rose in every survey year while lower-middle-income poverty fell.

plannedCharts.title: Depending on survey adjustment and poverty line, India's 2022-23 poverty rate was anywhere between 2.35% and 25.9%
plannedCharts.subtitle: Published 2022-23 Indian poverty headcount estimates across direct HCES (World Bank PIP) and survey-consistent imputation models (Himanshu, Lanjouw & Schirmer 2025)
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: Places the World Bank's unadjusted HCES headcounts next to academic imputation estimates that seek to account for the 2022-23 questionnaire and three-visit overhaul.

plannedCharts.title: Free public foodgrain and welfare items raise measured rural spending by 3.0%, against 1.2% in urban India
plannedCharts.subtitle: Average monthly per-capita consumption, with and without imputed free food and selected welfare goods · HCES 2023-24 published fact sheet
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: Shows the size of imputed public transfers using published rural and urban averages.

plannedCharts.title: The poorest surveyed tenth gained 13.1% in real consumption between the two comparable HCES rounds
plannedCharts.subtitle: Average real consumption by survey decile · HCES 2022-23 to 2023-24 · PIP comparable spell 2022-2023
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: Shows which parts of the measured distribution gained within the two explicitly comparable rounds.

plannedCharts.title: National Accounts spending grew 4.49x since 1977 while survey mean grew 2.09x
plannedCharts.subtitle: Indexed real per-capita growth in GDP, National Accounts Household Final Consumption Expenditure (HFCE), and NSS/HCES survey mean consumption · 1977 to 2023 (1977 = 100) · World Bank PIP
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: Shows the divergence between macro National Accounts and household surveys; it cannot identify the source of the gap or measure missing top-end consumption.

plannedCharts.title: Between 2003 and 2024, adult employment rates in poor Indian households fell to 58.3% while rising to 57.6% among the non-poor
plannedCharts.subtitle: Employment rate of working-age adults (15-64) and share of workers lacking secondary education by household poverty status (<$8.30/day vs >=$8.30/day), 2003 vs 2024 · World Bank 3PR Chapter 4
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: Extracts the core finding of Chapter 4 ('Jobs at the Center of Poverty Eradication'): poor Indian households have expanded schooling over twenty years, yet their adult employment rate declined.

plannedCharts.title: Paid employees below $3/day work 44.1 hours a week, against 44.9 above the line
plannedCharts.subtitle: Weekly hours in paid and self/unpaid work by household poverty status at $3/day · India, 2024 · World Bank Chapter 4, Box 4.1
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: Compares hours among employed people on either side of the $3/day household-consumption line.

plannedCharts.title: World Bank simulation: Closing India's employment and worker earnings gaps cuts $8.30 poverty by 22.2 percentage points
plannedCharts.subtitle: Combined employment and worker-earnings counterfactual · India, 2024 · World Bank Chapter 4
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: Shows the combined accounting counterfactual, not a causal policy payoff.

plannedCharts.title: Monetary poverty and deprivation measure different things: 35.5% of children were stunted in NFHS-5
plannedCharts.subtitle: Different denominators and vintages: HCES 2022-23/2023-24 poverty, NFHS-5 child nutrition (2019-21), health-spending hardship (2022)
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: Shows what household expenditure surveys miss: non-market capability deficits in sanitation, schooling, child nutrition, and catastrophic out-of-pocket medical bills.

plannedCharts.title: India has lower $3 poverty than Bangladesh and Indonesia, and higher poverty at $8.30
plannedCharts.subtitle: Selected Asian countries at the same three lines · 2024 calendar year · 2021 PPP · Indonesia actual, others projection/lineup
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: Tests the impression of success against neighbouring consumption distributions at common thresholds.

selectionRules: Start from the page question, not from the indicator name.
Choose the smallest set of visuals that explains scale, trend, structure, comparison, and caveat.
Prefer mobile-friendly charts: line charts with sparse ticks, horizontal bars, share strips, pyramids only when essential, and no dense tables.
Use one strong pull quote only when the evidence supports it with a number.
Add glossary blocks for technical terms that normal readers may not know.
caveats: Use only figures present in lockedNumbers or sourceSummaries.
If a related theme indicator is present, you may use it for context, but do not pretend it is the main answer.
If source coverage is thin, say so directly.
Do not compare states, districts, or cities unless the evidence packet contains those geographies.
forbiddenClaims: Do not infer causality from a trend unless the evidence explicitly supports it.
Do not cite a source that is not present in sourceSummaries.
